Most couches last **7 to 15 years**, and the spread is almost entirely explained by three things: the frame, the cushion fill, and how hard the household uses it. A kiln-dried hardwood frame with high-resilience foam in a quiet home can pass 15. A particleboard frame with low-density foam under two kids and a dog is often done by year five.

## Lifespan by Construction

| Component | Budget build | Mid-range | Quality build |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Frame | Particleboard, stapled: 3 to 7 yrs | Plywood or softwood: 7 to 12 yrs | Kiln-dried hardwood, doweled: 15 to 25+ yrs |
| Cushion fill | Low-density foam: 2 to 5 yrs before sag | Standard foam: 5 to 8 yrs | High-resilience foam or down blend: 10+ yrs |
| Suspension | Webbing: 5 to 8 yrs | Sinuous springs: 10 to 15 yrs | Eight-way hand-tied: 20+ yrs |
| Upholstery | Thin polyester: 3 to 5 yrs | Microfiber, performance fabric: 7 to 12 yrs | Top-grain leather: 15 to 25 yrs |

The weakest component sets the clock. A hardwood frame under foam that collapsed in year four is a four-year couch unless you replace the cushions.

## Signs It's Actually Done

- **Frame noise or flex.** Creaking, a visible lean, or a seat that bottoms out means structural failure. Cushions can be replaced; frames rarely are.
- **Permanent sag that cushion flipping doesn't fix.** Foam has lost its cell structure. Recovery isn't coming.
- **Odor that survives cleaning**, which means the foam has absorbed it. Our [pet-odor guide](/blog/home-cleaning/how-to-get-pet-odors-out-of-sofas-and-rugs/) covers when that's final.
- **Allergy symptoms that track to the couch.** Years of accumulated dander and dust-mite allergen in foam no cleaning reaches. See [the allergen guide](/blog/home-cleaning/how-to-remove-allergens-from-couch/).
- **Any moisture or mold history.** [Mold in foam is a replace decision](/blog/home-cleaning/moldy-couch-removal-tips-when-to-replace/), not a cleaning project.

## Repair, Replace, or Rehome

**Repair** when the frame is sound and the failure is cushions, a single spring, or a tear on a quality piece. New cushion inserts cost a fraction of a new couch. **Replace** when the frame is compromised or the piece was budget construction to begin with. **Rehome** when the couch is simply no longer yours in style or size but still sound: [charities take sofas in good condition](/blog/eco-friendly-living/can-couch-be-donated/), and a sound couch still has [resale value](/blog/home-cleaning/how-much-is-a-used-couch-worth/).

When replacement wins, [removal starts at $90](/pricing/) with the old couch carried out the same day the new one arrives.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How often should you replace a couch?

Every 7 to 15 years for most households. Quality construction and light use push toward 15 or beyond; budget construction, pets, and kids pull toward 5 to 7.

### Can an old couch be made like new?

If the frame is sound, yes to a point: new cushion inserts and professional cleaning restore comfort and appearance. Frame damage and absorbed odors are the two things that can't be undone.

### How do I know if my couch frame is broken?

Creaking when you sit, a visible lean, a seat that sinks to the base, or arms that wobble. Lift one corner a few inches: a sound frame stays rigid, a failed one flexes.

### Is it worth repairing a 10-year-old couch?

Worth it for a quality frame with worn cushions or fabric. Not worth it for budget construction, which usually has frame or suspension fatigue by then that repair can't address economically.
